clue.text: See 9
John has to put up key capital

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, as is bog

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up means writing it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A man called John has to raise the key to a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital city of Colombia.

clue.text: Spies have No 2 meeting head of KGB on board ship

indicators.note: things on board a ship are inside it, so these letters sit between its two letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
number two is a nursery word for faeces, here poo

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Secret agents meet their deputy and a Soviet intelligence chief aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: No 2 looks like a deputy in the spy ring; it is the childish word for excrement. 'meeting' just joins POO and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is informal for a spy or secret agent, so spies are spooks.

clue.text: Removing last of clothes, tried sex act in new positions, then disentangled

indicators.note: the remaining letters are placed in new positions, a rearrangement
removing means the following letter is taken out of the fodder
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A racy scene: clothes come off, a new sexual position is tried, then the couple untangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing last of clothes' takes the S (end of clothes) out of TRIED SEX ACT; the remaining ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free from an entanglement, so extricated means freed or disentangled.

clue.text: Colour screen

explanation.definitionFit: Shade is both a hue (noun) and a verb meaning to shield from the light.

clue.text: Victor is in dreadful poor condition

indicators.note: in places the victor letters inside the rearranged ones
dreadful suggests the word poor is in a bad state, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone named Victor is in a dreadful state of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges POOR to PROO, and VIS goes in to make PRO-VIS-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or stipulation attached to an agreement.

clue.text: A sink tap I ordered for a neighbour of No 14

indicators.note: the letters of a sink tap I are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone orders a new sink tap; the No 14 neighbour reads like a house number.
explanation.walkthrough: No 14 is 14-across, AFGHANISTAN, not a house; a person from the country next door fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakistan borders Afghanistan, so a citizen of Pakistan is a national of a neighbouring country.

clue.text: Starting late, boy eats up fillet of lemon sole

indicators.note: eats means the trimmed word takes the next letters inside it
starting late means the word boy begins one letter later, losing its opening letter
in a down clue up means the letters are written from bottom to top
to fillet is to take out the inside, so just the end letters of lemon remain

explanation.surface: A latecomer tucks into a fillet of lemon sole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lemon sole' looks like the fish, and 'fillet' like a cut of it; sole by itself is the definition, and filleting strips the word lemon to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and only both mean single, the one and no other.

clue.text: Foolishness only takes a second to turn into madness

indicators.note: takes means the first word receives the next letter into it

parts.note: inanity is silliness or foolishness

explanation.surface: A proverb: silliness can tip over into madness in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanity is a synonym of madness, mental derangement.

clue.text: Ex-husband meets relative in former stamping ground

parts.note: ex means old or former
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A divorced man meets his aunt at the place he used to frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamping ground is a place one used to frequent, which an old haunt is.

clue.text: Funny film's got her heaving bosom in first of shots

indicators.note: in places the bosom word inside the rearranged letters
heaving suggests tossing up and down, so the letters of 's got her are rearranged

parts.note: bosom means bust

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A comic film shows a woman's heaving bosom in its opening shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive 's joins GOT HER in the anagram, giving GHOSTER around BUST. Ghostbusters fits the puzzle's theme of ghostly film titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghostbusters is a 1984 supernatural comedy film starring Bill Murray and Dan Aykroyd.

clue.text: Like salad could be made more basic!

indicators.note: could be signals that the words like salad can become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether their dish, like the salad, could be simpler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basic' looks like simple; in chemistry a base is the opposite of an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: To alkalise is to make a substance alkaline, that is more basic in chemistry.

clue.text: One goes in to have meal with Sally on vacation to relax

indicators.note: goes in means the numeral is put inside the phrase for having a meal

parts.note: to have a meal is to take tea
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: on vacation means the word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone goes in to have a meal with their friend Sally and unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking tea is the British habit of a light afternoon meal; 'goes in' slips the numeral one inside that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To take it easy is an idiom for to rest or relax.

clue.text: Girl has old 5d coin that's the same on both sides

definitions.text: old 5d coin that's the same on both sides
definitions.meaning: a former coin of Pakistan and India, and the word reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A girl holds an old coin with identical faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 5d is PAKISTANI; 'the same on both sides' seems to describe the coin's faces but says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a sixteenth of a rupee in British India and Pakistan; Anna is also a common female name.

clue.text: Girl nonetheless consumed 19 for example

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
still means nonetheless or even so
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A girl ate something despite everything, then is pointed to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is 19-down, SPIRIT: a spirit is made by distillation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits such as whisky are distilled, so a spirit is an example of a distilled liquid.

clue.text: Country coat is brown

parts.note: an afghan is a sheepskin coat with the fleece inside
tan is a yellowish brown

explanation.surface: Someone's coat is brown.
explanation.walkthrough: An afghan coat was a 1970s fashion item.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghanistan is a landlocked country in Central and South Asia.

clue.text: I'm staging reconstruction to generate excessive growth

indicators.note: reconstruction means the letters of the phrase are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A director stages a reconstruction to drum up a big expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantism is abnormal, excessive growth of the body.

clue.text: Goes faster with drug and drink

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone accelerates after taking drugs and alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeds up is a phrasal verb meaning accelerates.

clue.text: A broken love needing time's soothing balm

indicators.note: broken means the letters of a love are shattered and reset

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A broken heart needs time, the great healer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera gel is a plant extract applied to soothe burns and skin.

clue.text: Cast let priest go in scary movie

indicators.note: cast suggests throwing, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A film's cast lets the priest go from a horror movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the film's actors; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Poltergeist is a 1982 horror film about a haunted family home.

clue.text: Liquor, a bit of rum I poured into gob

indicators.note: poured into means these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: to gob is to spit

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tot of rum is poured into someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gob' looks like the British slang for mouth; here it is the verb to spit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is distilled alcoholic drink such as whisky or rum, which is liquor.

clue.text: Fellow on top of hill gets cooler

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of means the first piece is written above the second

parts.note: a ridge is a long hill

explanation.surface: A man on a hilltop finds it chillier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fridge is a refrigerator, an appliance that keeps food cool.

clue.text: Keep everything back inside fence with it

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
inside says the letters are found within the words keep everything

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An order to keep all belongings back within the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'inside' into the definition, but it signals the hidden letters; 'fence with it' alone defines the sword. 'back' reverses EEPE from kEEP Everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword, the weapon used in one form of fencing.

clue.text: Bury has Lancashire's foremost musical show cut short by uninvited guest

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of Lancashire
cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an opera is a musical show

explanation.surface: The town of Bury hosts Lancashire's leading musical, ended early by a gatecrasher.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town but is the verb to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is an intruder, someone who turns up where not wanted.

clue.text: Leader of 7 getting drastically demoted, quits …

indicators.note: drastically demoted means the leading letter drops all the way to the bottom

parts.note: the number seven written as a word

explanation.surface: The leader of a team of seven is harshly demoted and resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of 7' looks like 7-down; it means the S at the head of SEVEN, which moves to the end. 'quits' is not resigns but square.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means being even, with no debt on either side.

clue.text: … bank and is just not able

definitions.meaning: to tilt or bank, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: Continuing 23: the bank is simply unable to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant means tilt or slope; with an apostrophe the same letters say cannot.

clue.text: Move over as pet dies unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of as pet dies are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sad scene: make room as the family pet passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: To step aside is to move out of the way or make room.

clue.text: Broadcast first class action comedy film

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I
RED is a 2010 action comedy film starring Bruce Willis

explanation.surface: A top-quality action comedy is shown on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Aired means broadcast, transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: Solo pilot's first to go in front. Cruise in jet

indicators.note: to go in front puts that letter before the next name
first means the opening letter of pilot

parts.note: Han Solo is the pilot in Star Wars
Tom Cruise, the film star

explanation.surface: Han Solo the pilot gives way, and Tom Cruise flies a jet in Top Gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The F-4 Phantom is a military jet fighter aircraft.

clue.text: Good man pulls muscle in soldier/spy movie

indicators.note: pulls ... in means the first word draws the next into its middle
in completes pulls ... in, putting the muscle inside

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
pec is short for pectoral muscle
RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier

explanation.surface: A decent soldier strains a muscle filming a spy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulls muscle' reads as an injury; 'pulls ... in' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectre is the 2015 James Bond spy film.
